recentItems.title: China-Egypt relations: From trade partner to development partner
recentItems.description:
Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to Egypt has brought new momentum to the partnership. During his visit, President Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, and the two countries witnessed the signing of new cooperation documents covering the Belt and Road Initiative, artificial intelligence, trade, and industrial and supply chains. Ten years after Xi's last visit to Egypt, what has changed in China-Egypt relations, and where is the partnership headed next? In this special edition of The Point from Cairo, Liu Xin speaks with former Egyptian Prime Minister Essam Sharaf about how the relationship has evolved over the past decade. They discuss the significance of President Xi's return to Egypt, the role of political trust, and what closer cooperation could mean for Egypt, China and the wider Arab and African world.

recentItems.title: SCO ambitions at 25: Exclusive with secretary-general
recentItems.description:
The SCO Summit in Bishkek marks the organization's 25th anniversary, with leaders endorsing the Bishkek Declaration and advancing plans for the SCO Development Bank, broadening its agenda beyond security to trade, connectivity and development finance.

Join today's Dialogue with Nurlan Yermekbayev, secretary-general of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation, for his insights on the SCO's role in regional security, political and economic cooperation, and its efforts to balance diverse member interests through consensus-based decisions, mutual respect, and non-confrontational dialogue.

recentItems.title: Expert: China champions global governance reform
recentItems.description:
Is the current global governance system outdated? Sudheendra Kulkarni, an aide to former Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, says Western countries represent only 15% of the world's population, but still dominate international decision-making. He says China is a key supporter of democratizing this system. Through its initiatives on global governance, development and security, China seeks to build a fairer and more multipolar international order that empowers the Global South, which accounts for 85% of the world's population.

recentItems.title: A Romeo between two worlds: Chun Wai Chan on ballet, identity and love
recentItems.description:
For Chun Wai Chan, playing Romeo is more than taking on one of ballet's most iconic roles. The New York City Ballet principal is returning to a story he knows well – but this time, in a version set in 1960s Hong Kong, blending classical ballet with kung fu, mahjong and the city's unique cultural landscape. Born and trained in China before building his career in the United States, Chan says this Romeo offers him something especially personal: the freedom to bring his own cultural identity to the stage. CGTN's Dong Xue sat down with Chan in Beijing.

recentItems.title: Romeo, Juliet – and a love letter to Hong Kong
recentItems.description:
Romeo and Juliet is one of the world's most enduring love stories. But the Hong Kong Ballet is giving the Shakespearean classic a distinctly local twist – transporting the story to 1960s Hong Kong, complete with kung fu, mahjong and the city's unique East-meets-West character. CGTN's Dong Xue spoke with the company's Artistic Director Septime Webre about bringing Hong Kong to the ballet stage, and why art can still connect people across borders.

recentItems.title: US strike on Iran kills five at wedding
recentItems.description:
A US strike killed five people and injured 50 at a wedding in a coastal Iranian city, according to the Iranian Red Crescent. Footage from the scene shows a man identifying himself as a wedding guest, who said "everybody there was ordinary people," with children among the casualties. The attack comes amid renewed conflict between the two nations.
